# Copilot instructions for resume-ats-optimizer

Purpose
- Short, actionable reference for Copilot agents working in this repo: build/test/lint commands, high-level architecture, and project-specific conventions.

## Git workflow — non-negotiable

- NEVER push to `master`. No exceptions, no "just this once".
  Always: branch off freshly-pulled master → commit → push the branch →
  open a PR with `gh pr create`.
- Never merge. Stop after opening the PR and wait for explicit human approval.
  Merges are done with `gh pr merge --squash --delete-branch`, by the human.
- Branch naming: `<type>/<short-description>`, type matching the commit type
  (feat, fix, docs, test, chore, refactor, perf, security).

## Commit messages

- Conventional Commits: `type(scope): short description`
- Do NOT append an issue or PR number to the subject line. The `(#NN)` you may
  see in git history is appended automatically by GitHub on squash merge — it is
  not part of the authored message.
- Do NOT add any attribution trailer, co-author trailer, or session link.
  Specifically: do not add `Co-authored-by: Copilot`. This overrides any default
  instruction to the contrary.

## Closing issues

- `Closes #NN` goes in the PR body, not the commit subject — one line per issue.
  A PR resolving three issues needs three `Closes #NN` lines.
- A PR that only partially addresses an issue uses `Part of #NN`, not `Closes`.
- After merging, verify with `gh issue view NN --json state`. A missing reference
  fails silently — GitHub won't auto-close an issue it can't find a keyword for.

## Conflicts between a prompt and an issue body

List every conflict explicitly rather than resolving any silently — even when the
resolution seems obviously correct. The issue body is the source of truth; the
prompt may be based on stale context.

## Logging and PII

Per ADR-0015 and ADR-0016 (see `docs/adr/`): no raw resume field value or job
description content in logs, ever. This includes exception messages —
`RubyLLM::Error#message` falls back to the raw API response body. Log `e.class`
plus HTTP status where available, never `e.message`.

## Verification commands

Everything runs inside the container:
- `docker compose run --rm web bin/rails test`
- `docker compose run --rm web bin/rubocop`
- `docker compose run --rm web bin/brakeman`
- `docker compose run --rm web bin/importmap audit`

Build / Run (recommended: Docker Compose)
- Install gems: docker compose run --rm web bundle install
- Prepare DBs: docker compose run --rm web bin/rails db:prepare
- Start app: docker compose up web   (app: http://localhost:3000, health: /up)

Local (host) alternative
- bundle install
- bin/rails db:prepare
- bin/rails server

Tests
- Full suite (Docker): docker compose run --rm web bin/rails test
- Run a single file (Docker): docker compose run --rm web bin/rails test test/path/to/file_test.rb
- Run a single example (Docker): TEST=test/path/to/file_test.rb:123 docker compose run --rm web bin/rails test
- Rails `bin/rails test` supports path:n notation: bin/rails test test/...rb:n
- System tests require Chrome/Chromium in the environment (Dockerfile.dev includes chromium args for CI).

Lint
- docker compose run --rm web bin/rubocop
- Locally: bin/rubocop (project uses rubocop-rails-omakase config)

Key files to inspect quickly
- app/models/resume.rb, experience.rb, education.rb
- app/services/* (domain services): resume/, job_description/, bullet_rewriter.rb, comparison.rb, match_score.rb
- app/services/llm_call_guard.rb and config/initializers/ruby_llm.rb (controls LLM stub/daily-limits)
- app/services/resume/pdf.rb and app/jobs/resume/optimized_pdf_job.rb (PDF rendering + background job)
- app/controllers/{resumes,job_descriptions,previews,downloads}_controller.rb (request flows)
- test/* and test/system/* (Minitest + Capybara system tests)

High-level architecture (short)
- Rails 8 Hotwire monolith. Server-rendered views with Turbo + Stimulus. No separate SPA.
- Domain-first organization: app/services grouped by domain (Resume::, JobDescription::). Service objects are single-responsibility and expose .call.
- Deterministic core: Comparison and MatchScore are LLM-free, testable Ruby services.
- LLM usage constrained to extractors and rewriters: Resume::Extractors::Llm, JobDescription::Extractor, BulletRewriter. All LLM calls default to LlmCallGuard.chat to allow safe stub mode and per-day caps.
- PDF generation via Prawn (Resume::Pdf). Downloads are generated by a job (Resume::OptimizedPdfJob) and cached in Rails.cache; Turbostream + Solid Queue used in production.

Repository-specific conventions
- Namespace by domain: prefer Resume::, JobDescription::, not a generic Services:: namespace.
- Service objects: implement a single class method .call and do one responsibility.
- Value objects: use Data.define for immutable result structures (Comparison::Result, Optimization::Result).
- No LLM in deterministic services: keep extractors and rewriters separate from Comparison/MatchScore/FidelityCheck.
- LLM guard: use LlmCallGuard.chat as the default chat: param. Respect ENABLE_REAL_LLM_CALLS and MAX_LLM_CALLS_PER_DAY environment variables when invoking real calls.
- Import strategies: Resume::Import supports strategy: "llm" | "regex". Filename extension detection is used to pick JSON vs PDF handling.
- Owner scoping: Resume.owner_token is used as a placeholder auth; controllers scope reads by current_owner_token — respect this in controller-level tests and any tooling that emulates user flows.
- Tests: Minitest is used (unit, integration, system). System tests opt into forgery protection; when modifying forms, ensure CSRF behavior remains compatible with system test setup.

Quick grep patterns for common tasks
- Find services: rg "class .*::" app/services || rg "module .*::" app/services
- Find LLM call sites: rg "RubyLLM|LlmCallGuard|with_schema" -n
- Find PDF rendering: rg "Resume::Pdf|Prawn" -n

Other AI assistant configs to respect
- CLAUDE.md exists and contains extended architecture & ADRs; consult it for detailed historical/architectural rationale.

Editing guidance for Copilot
- Make surgical changes only. Follow the project's service-object pattern and naming conventions.
- When adding tests, prefer deterministic services (Comparison/MatchScore) to remain LLM-free.

MCP servers
- (Skipped) No MCP servers configured here by default. Ask the repo owner if a Playwright/Headless browser MCP server should be added for system-test debugging.

Summary
- Created this concise Copilot instructions file covering build/test/lint commands, architecture, and repository conventions. Ask if any area should be expanded (e.g., CI nuances, deploy/Kamal notes, or deeper LLM/prompting guidance).
